cards.headline: Winnie the Pooh-themed high tea at SKAI; free VR dance-storytelling experience at libraries
bullets: Enjoy Winnie the Pooh high tea at SKAI until Aug 31.
Experience a free VR dance-storytelling adventure at libraries until Aug 2.
The Pooh high tea celebrates the book series' 100th anniversary.
VR experience is based on the Sang Kancil folktale.

cards.headline: Growing up together: Pre-school giants venture into after-school care for primary school pupils
bullets: Big pre-school names like MindChamps and MapleBear are now offering after-school care for primary kids.
These new centres aim to support families and kids beyond pre-school years.
The new after-school programmes are pricier, costing around $900 monthly.
This is much higher than the average $290 monthly fee for registered student care centres.

cards.headline: MDDI to have group discussion with parents, hear views on plans to make social media safer for kids
bullets: 81% of parents worry about kids seeing bad stuff online, a recent survey found.
The government wants parents' views on making social media safer for children.
A discussion on July 25 will gather ideas on rules for kids using social media.
New rules already require platforms to block harmful content and app stores to stop kids downloading bad apps.

cards.headline: Bears rescued from Laos farm step outdoors for the first time after rescue led by S’porean
bullets: 27 bears rescued from a Laos bile farm are now exploring a new sanctuary.
A Singaporean led the rescue of the bears, who were kept in cages for years.
The bears are learning to climb trees and eat real food for the first time.
Some bears are now in a large forested area with pools, while others wait for new enclosures.

cards.headline: Why unreasonable behaviour is the top reason cited for divorce in S’pore, and adultery the least
bullets: Nearly half of civil divorces in 2025 cited unreasonable behaviour as the main reason.
Adultery was the least common reason for civil divorces, at only 0.9 per cent.
Muslim divorces cited infidelity more often, but lawyers say this is due to different laws.
Unreasonable behaviour covers many issues like abuse, neglect, and financial problems.
Proving adultery in civil court is often difficult and costly for couples.

cards.headline: Annual leave for outsourced Progressive Wage Model workers to increase from 7 to 10 days progressively from 2029
bullets: Outsourced workers under the Progressive Wage Model will get more annual leave days.
Their minimum annual leave will rise from 7 to 10 days.
This change will happen gradually starting in 2029.
About 60 per cent of these workers are expected to benefit.
The move aims to recognise their long service even if employers change.

cards.headline: Singaporean arrested after Jakarta police bust etomidate vape factory: Reports
bullets: Jakarta police busted an etomidate vape factory and arrested a Singaporean man.
Thousands of vape cartridges and equipment were seized in the North Jakarta raid.
The 34-year-old suspect allegedly aimed to make 500 vape cartridges daily.
Airport customs had previously seized 2.2kg of etomidate.

cards.headline: No discrepancy found in O-Level English oral exam questions: SEAB
bullets: SEAB confirmed O-Level English oral exam questions were the same for everyone.
Complaints online suggested screen questions differed for candidates and examiners.
SEAB investigated after feedback about possible exam question discrepancies.
Some candidates admitted they misread the prompts initially, SEAB noted.

cards.headline: Approved fosterers may keep up to 6 cats in HDB flats, 10 in private homes under new pilot scheme
bullets: Approved cat fosterers can keep up to six cats in HDB flats and ten in private homes.
This new limit is part of a two-year pilot scheme starting August 3, 2026.
All foster cats must be sterilised, and licensing fees will be waived during the pilot.
Existing pet cats exceeding current limits can stay if licensed during the transition.

cards.headline: Singapore chefs cook up chilli crab, laksa and chicken rice for 180 diners in Peru
bullets: Singapore chefs cooked chilli crab, laksa, and chicken rice for 180 people in Peru.
They brought 70kg of ingredients from Singapore to Peru for the event.
The dinner was the first big showcase of Singaporean food in Peru's capital.
Chefs aimed to share Singapore's unique flavours with a new audience abroad.

cards.headline: World Cup: England take third place with 6-4 win against France
bullets: England beat France 6-4 to take third place in the World Cup.
Bukayo Saka scored three goals for England.
The 10 goals scored was a record for a third-place playoff match.
Kylian Mbappe scored twice, becoming the World Cup's all-time top scorer.

cards.headline: England manager Tuchel has no regrets over World Cup semi-final decisions
bullets: England will play France on Sunday morning for third place in the World Cup.
Manager Tuchel has no regrets about his decisions in the semi-final loss to Argentina.
He believes his team became too passive after taking the lead.
Tuchel says the team's fatigue from previous matches might have played a role.

cards.headline: Lamborghini Temerario review: A reckless decision, but one you won’t regret
bullets: The new Lamborghini Temerario has 920 horsepower and hits 100 kmh in 2.7 seconds.
This hybrid supercar uses a V8 engine and electric motors for four-wheel drive.
It can drive silently for short distances using only electric power.
The car costs S$1,528,000 before adding any optional extras.
Despite the high price, the car offers an exciting and emotional driving experience.

cards.headline: US housing starts rebound on multifamily construction
bullets: US housing starts jumped 19% in June, reaching the highest level since March.
Apartment construction saw a big comeback, rising over 76% last month.
However, new single-family home construction saw a slight dip.
This rebound shows how much monthly housing numbers can change.

cards.headline: Most buyers of million-dollar HDB flats paid no COV in 2025: PropNex
bullets: Most buyers of million-dollar HDB flats did not pay extra cash over valuation.
About 69% of buyers paid no cash over valuation for these million-dollar flats.
Buyers aged 30 to 49 made up 71% of those buying million-dollar HDB flats.
Retirees aged 60 and above bought these flats as their next home after selling private property.
About 1,002 HDB flats sold for at least S$1 million so far this year.

cards.headline: Housing plan at site within Maju Forest not final: HDB chief town planner
bullets: HDB says housing plans for Maju Forest site are not final yet.
Over 100 residents met HDB and MPs to discuss housing plans.
Concerns about deforestation and traffic were raised by residents.
HDB is looking at Maju Forest for housing due to high demand.
Feedback on the housing plans can be submitted until August 2026.

cards.headline: Approved cat fosterers can keep up to 6 cats in HDB flats & 10 in private premises from Aug. 3 under pilot scheme
bullets: From Aug. 3, approved cat fosterers can keep up to 6 cats in HDB flats.
They can keep up to 10 cats in private homes under a new pilot scheme.
The new rules include both pet and fostered cats in the home.
Licensing fees will be waived for approved fosterers during the two-year pilot.

cards.headline: Man, 69, says someone threw canned mushrooms & baked beans from block onto his new Toyota car causing dents
bullets: Two cans of mushrooms and baked beans fell from a HDB block, denting a new Toyota car.
The incident happened overnight at a Bedok North car park.
The car owner found the damage the next morning and filed a police report.
The car repair cost S$3,000, with the owner paying S$600 from his own pocket.
The owner now parks elsewhere to avoid further incidents.

cards.headline: This Walkathon Takes You Through 3 RWS Attractions Before The Crowds, Join A Breakfast Rave Too
bullets: Walk through Universal Studios Singapore, Oceanarium, and Adventure Cove before crowds at a 1.4km charity walk.
The walkathon on August 22nd supports President's Challenge, with RWS matching all funds raised.
Meet characters like Minions and Kung Fu Panda along the route.
Your ticket includes a breakfast rave with DJ Jasmine Red and a full day at Adventure Cove Waterpark.
President Tharman Shanmugaratnam will attend the festival opening.

cards.headline: What Would You Do With Spider-Man’s Powers In SG? We Asked Local Youths To Share
bullets: Local youths shared what they'd do with Spider-Man's powers, mostly for convenience, not crime-fighting.
Many said they'd use powers to skip traffic jams and avoid crowded MRT rides.
Some would use abilities to rescue people or pets stuck in high places.
Others joked about using powers to ace IPPT or get the best concert seats.
A Spider-Man themed mural is being painted at *SCAPE until July 22.

cards.headline: Marina Square Has An SG-Themed Sanrio Pop-Up, With Nostalgic Photo Ops & Exclusive Merch
bullets: Marina Square is hosting a free Sanrio pop-up until August 16, 2026.
The pop-up features Singapore-themed photo spots and exclusive Sanrio merchandise.
You can buy Sanrio T-shirts starting from $29 and Mr. Merlion plushies for $39.
Spend $100 to redeem an exclusive Sanrio characters enamel mug.
Post on Instagram and tag accounts to get a free Sanrio sticker set.
